UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                            BEFORE THE
              FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


Southwest Power Pool, Inc.                                      Docket No. ER26-3685-000


    MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS OF THE SOUTHWEST
            POWER POOL MARKET MONITORING UNIT
       The Market Monitoring Unit (Market Monitor) of the Southwest Power Pool (SPP)

respectfully moves to intervene1 and submits these comments in support of SPP’s proposed

revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff) filed on September 2, 2026, and

titled “Submission of Tariff Revisions to Clarify the Conditional High Impact Large Load

Policy” (Filing).2 The Market Monitor views these proposed Tariff revisions, in

conjunction with other related changes SPP has made to various governing documents, as

important for helping to better clarify the sequencing of curtailing Conditional High Impact

Large Loads (CHILLs).


1
  The Market Monitor moves to intervene pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy
Regulatory Commission’s (FERC or Commission) Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 C.F.R. §§
385.212, 385.214), and in fulfillment of its responsibilities under Commission Order No. 719
(Wholesale Competition in Regions with Organized Electric Markets, Order No. 719, FERC
Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,281, at P 354 (2008) (Order No. 719), order on reh’g, Order No. 719-A,
FERC Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,292, order on reh’g, Order No. 719-B, 129 FERC ¶ 61,252 (2009))
and Attachment AG of the SPP Tariff (Southwest Power Pool, Inc., FERC Electric Tariff, Sixth
Revised Volume No. 1, Attachment AG, § 6.2 (SPP Tariff)). As SPP’s independent market
monitor, the Market Monitor is required under the provisions of the SPP Tariff to monitor and
evaluate the efficiency and competitiveness of SPP’s markets and services. The Market Monitor
has a direct and substantial interest in the outcome of this proceeding that cannot be adequately
represented by any other entity. The Market Monitor’s intervention and participation in this
proceeding is in the public interest. For these reasons, the Market Monitor respectfully requests
that it be permitted to intervene in this proceeding with full rights as a party.
2
  Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Submission of Tariff Revisions to Clarify the Conditional High
Impact Large Load Policy, Docket No. ER26-3685-000 (September 2, 2026) (Filing).
        During the stakeholder process for the Conditional High Impact Large Load Service

(CHILLS) proposal3, the MMU made several recommendations to improve and further

specify the processes and requirements around the curtailment of CHILLs.4 Among these

recommendations were that SPP should 1) clarify and document the sequencing of CHILL

curtailments in relation to reliability commitments and deployment of reliability registered

demand response programs and 2) create clear expectations for how quickly CHILLs must

be able to curtail when instructed.

       The Filing provides straightforward, clarifying changes to the parts of the Tariff that

outline CHILL curtailments/reductions in the Day-Ahead Market and Reliability Unit

Commitment (RUC) processes. For example, as described in the Filing, in Section 5.2.2(3)

of Attachment AE of the Tariff, the Day-Ahead RUC process will initially check the

eligibility of CHILLs and recommend CHILL curtailments. It will then proceed through

the remainder of the Day-Ahead RUC execution steps, and if it encounters insufficient

capacity to meet system load and operating reserves, then CHILLs that had passed the

initial check (e.g., CHILLs with paired generation) may potentially still be curtailed. In

addition to these relatively minor Tariff revisions, SPP has also updated its Emergency




3
  Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Revisions to Add Conditional High Impact Large Load Service,
Docket No. ER26-1323-000 (February 10, 2026)

 Operating Plan and Operating Criteria to further specify where the curtailment of CHILLs

fits within the order of operations taken to address reliability issues.5

       As part of the Revision Request6 that contains the proposed Tariff changes presented

in this Filing, SPP is also modifying its Integrated Marketplace Protocols to include some

additional clarity on how quickly CHILLs must curtail when instructed.7 We are supportive

of these efforts to better define the rules and steps involved in curtailing CHILLs.

       As CHILLs begin to connect to the SPP system, we anticipate that there will be

considerable operational experience and knowledge gained on how best to effectively

manage these new, non-firm, large loads. In turn, further modifications and refinements to

the processes used to curtail CHILLs may be warranted in the future. The Market Monitor

appreciates the opportunity to offer comments on the proposed changes in this Filing and

recommends that the Commission approve the requested Tariff revisions.
